subject: Access list elements with numeric names in a loop?

messages.author: 03c3aeeb0cc6692c
messages.subject: Access list elements with numeric names in a loop?
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I have a list with numeric names such as:

names(mylist)
  [1]  "2"     "3"     "4"     "6"     "8"     "9" 

and I want to be able to select the elements in the list based on a group of the numeric names like:
group1 <- (4, 6,8)

and then eventually unlist the elements and save them in a vector. 

I tried this:
emptyvec <- vector()
for (i in group1){
  emptyvec <- append(emptyvec,unlist(mylist$'i')) 
}

but it returns an empty vector. I also tried converting the group1 to character with as.character(), but this did not help. 

I can access the list elements directly with  mylist$'2' for example, but it does not see to work with indexing within the loop. I think I need to use a loop since my original list is very large, I have 15 groups, and each group has up to 28 elements. 

Thank you,
Katie 
--
--
Katherine Ransom
PhD Candidate
Hydrologic Sciences Graduate Group
UC Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Access list elements with numeric names in a loop?
parts:
Good points all! I just want to mention that loops aren't bad, it's how they get used that is often the issue. Basically, it is the incremental collection of results into a data frame which is really slow when using loops (especially for large data sets like Rosemary mentions). However functions like 'lapply' or packages such as data.table avoid that step, and can make loops incredibly fast.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Access list elements with numeric names in a loop?
parts:
Yep, I think that's a crucial point. A few other, miscellaneus things:

(1) There's a nice discussion of the "apply" family and friends at:

https://nsaunders.wordpress.com/2010/08/20/a-brief-introduction-to-apply-in-r/

(2) It is sometimes the case that you *can't* use an apply-like
function, if, for instance, you need to keep track of variables in the
previous iteration(s) of the loop. ("f[i] <- f[i - 1] + f[i - 2]")

(3) I don't know the details of this, but R has the flexibility to
have "x" represent "elephant" in one iteration of the loop and 42 in
the next. Hence, I think there's some unavoidable (?) overhead in a
loop as R checks the types, etc. This would be a good place for smart
people to jump in and comment.

(4) Assuming the effect in (3) is somehow present and relevant, I
wonder if the "compile" package:

https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/compiler/html/compile.html

could be used to reduce or eliminate that overhead.
